evidence.text: Apple's December-quarter iPhone guide faces a $85.3B (+23%) comp with no base iPhone 18 this fall. Nikkei (2026-10-09) reported October iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders cut 15-20% from Apple's original requests on soft demand; Securities Times says Pro Max +10-15% and Pro -10-15%, total flat. Counterpoint's first-three-weeks sell-through for the 18 Pro series is +3.1% globally (US -4%, Japan -27%, China +29%). Consensus December revenue of ~$152B (+5.7%) needs iPhone roughly flat to up on that comp.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line Apple trades on. July 2026: guide of 9-11% against ~12% expected, -7.3% next close (apexvol) after a beat. April 2026: guide of 14-17% above estimates, +3.2%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The order-cut story is public and the stock went on to a record close on 10-29, so the market largely looked through it. What is not priced is how Apple frames the comp in the guide. A priced version would show December consensus at or below Goldman's $151.2B rather than $152-153B. Put skew at the 86th percentile says some of this is hedged.
evidence.independence: Counterpoint 3-week sell-through, a different firm and dataset (https://www.neoteo.com/en/counterpoint-estimates-iphone-18-pro-sales-rose-31-globally-while-the-us-fell-4, 2026-10-28). Counterpoint China note expecting this generation to sell below the last in Q4 (https://counterpointresearch.com/en/insights/iphone-18-pro-series-sales-up-12-percent-yoy-in-launch-week-in-china-as-apple-takes-hashtag-1-spot, 2026-09-30). Counter-evidence is folded into the size: China +29% and total Pro orders flat per Securities Times (https://www.sammyfans.com/2026/10/10/apple-boosts-duo-and-pro-max-orders-while-cutting-iphone-18-pro-orders/amp/). Nikkei itself says a $100 higher Pro price means lower units do not immediately lower revenue.

evidence.text: iPhone Duo ($1,999, on sale 10-23) is supply-limited. BofA puts average delivery waits at 79 days, with shipments into January. Apple said on ~10-26/27 it will replace Duo units with inner-display cracks, and reports say replacement stock is drawing on already depleted inventory. So less Duo revenue lands in the December quarter than Counterpoint's ~6M-units-this-year figure implies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Supply-constraint commentary in the July 2026 guide was cited as a cause of the -7.3% move. Apple has historically guided through iPhone supply constraints (January 2026: 'currently constrained').
evidence.why_not_priced: The crack story broke 10-25 to 10-27. The stock still closed at a record on 10-29, so it was read as a product story, not a guide input. A priced version would show December revenue estimates trimmed after 10-27; the only cut on record is Goldman's, and it predates the replacements.
evidence.independence: Reuters preview citing BofA's 79-day wait and IDC's Popal on demand exceeding supply (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/apple-s-new-ceo-ternus-to-face-first-earnings-test-as-memory-costs-surge-ce785fd8dc88f42c, 2026-11-02). Apple's statement on replacements via KSL/AP (https://www.ksl.com/article/51641303/apple-says-it-will-replace-iphone-duo-units-showing-screen-problems). Two-sided: the shortage reflects demand above supply, so revenue is deferred rather than lost. Sized small for that reason.

evidence.text: Memory costs are still rising into the December quarter. SK hynix's Q3 2026 DRAM ASP was up high-20s % QoQ and it sees shortages through 2030. TrendForce sees Q4 conventional DRAM contracts +10-15% and Q3 mobile DRAM +8-13% QoQ, though it expects Q4 mobile increases to narrow. Apple said in July it expects 'to pay even higher memory costs', and its own Sept-quarter GM guide is ~46-47% ex-refunds. The December GM guide risks landing below Goldman's 46.8%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 sell-off was attributed to memory costs plus the guide (https://www.euronews.com/business/2026/07/31/apple-shares-fall-despite-record-revenue-as-outlook-disappoints).
evidence.why_not_priced: Every preview names memory, so the direction is priced. The level is not: no source carries a December GM consensus except Goldman's 46.8%. If the market had priced a sub-46% guide, Goldman's number would not be the low end of the visible range.
evidence.independence: TrendForce mobile DRAM 3Q26 report (https://www.trendforce.com/research/download/RP260803NC, 2026-08-03), a different firm. It also contains the counter-point that Q4 mobile increases narrow, folded into the size. CNBC on Apple's July comments (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/30/apple-earnings-live-updates.html).

evidence.text: Teradyne's 2026-10-06 launch of burn-in on its Titan HP platform set off the leg down (about $100 to $73 within a week, $53 now). The day after, 2026-10-07, Aehr's lead hyperscale Sonoma customer placed ~$6M of follow-on production orders for its next-generation AI processor, shipping to a Taiwan OSAT over six months. The 2026-11-02 call is management's first chance to address the competitive question in public. Titan HP is a package/system-level product; it overlaps Sonoma (about $50M of the FY27 guide per the CEO) more than FOX wafer-level burn-in.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a competitor. The closest precedent is the 2025-10-06 print (-17.38%), where the hyperscaler/AI deal news did not offset weak revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: The price holds the bear case. A ~$1.7B cap on a $130-150M guide after a 49% drop, with downside paid in the skew, is what a share-loss narrative looks like. If the market had absorbed the re-order and the wafer-level vs. package-level distinction, the stock would have stabilised after Oppenheimer's 2026-10-14 note; it fell another ~27%. That cuts both ways: the sell-side rebuttal is public and did not work, so only management's own words, or a reaffirmed or raised guide, can move it, and this finding is sized for that.
evidence.independence: Teradyne PR (https://stockhouse.com/news/press-releases/2026/10/06/teradyne-introduces-titan-hp-platform-with-burn-in-capabilities-for-advanced-ai, 2026-10-06; Titan HP 'available now and deployed in production'). evidence.text: Upstart pre-released Q3 2026 originations of $4,117.8m (Jul $1,397.4m, Aug $1,342.1m, Sep $1,378.3m), 2.6% below Q2's $4,227.2m. At Q2's fee take rate ($348.0m fees / $4,227.2m = 8.23%) that is about $339m of fees; adding Q2-like net interest and fair-value income of about $16m gives total revenue near $355m, about 2-3% below the $365m consensus, which sits flat on Q2. The 25bp Fed hike of 2026-09-16 also points to a negative fair-value mark on about $1.06bn of balance-sheet loans.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: originations $2.9bn against $3.3bn consensus and revenue $277m against $280m; the stock fell 14.8% (American Banker, 2025-11-05). Q2 2026: revenue $364.7m beat with the guide reaffirmed, and the stock went -0.4% on the day (baseline). Beats have not been paid; misses on volume have been punished.
evidence.why_not_priced: Originations are public, but a consensus of $365.5m (Benzinga) / $364.6m (Earnings Whispers) is flat on Q2 revenue while volume fell 2.6% q/q. That requires the take rate to rise about 20bp after a quarter whose rise the CFO credited to seasonality and mix, while saying she expected 'relative stability'. If estimates had absorbed the volume release, consensus revenue would sit near $355m, not $365m. Partly priced: the stock has fallen about 10% since the 10-05 release.
evidence.independence: Q2 fee and origination figures come from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001647639/000164763926000062/upst991prq22026.htm). evidence.text: The reaffirmed FY2026 guide needs a sharp H2 ramp. On revenue, $1.4bn less H1 $673m ($308m Q1 + $365m Q2) leaves $727m for H2. On adj. EBITDA, $294m less H1 $117.4m leaves $176.6m, against Q2's $76.9m. With Q3 volume down q/q and fixed costs guided up low single digits in Q3 and Q4, Q4 would need about $370m+ revenue and about $95m EBITDA. That makes a trim, or a guide hit only through an aggressive Q4, likely. The macro moved against the guide: the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 (its first hike since 2023) and 12 of 18 officials project another by year-end. A direct peer, Pagaya, implied a Q4 volume midpoint about 14% below Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven prints have produced this name's largest moves: Feb 2025 +31.8% on a strong initial guide; Aug 2025 -18.7% and Feb 2026 -15.0% on guide/take-rate disappointment (baseline). A reaffirm in Aug 2026 got -0.4% and then about -30% drift.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Street's Q3+Q4 EBITDA ($83.2m + $93.9m = $177m) still equals the guide exactly, which means estimates are anchored to the company number rather than to the post-hike rate path. If a cut were priced, consensus would sit below the guide. The stock at its 52-week low with +16.8 put skew does show the market fears it, so part of this is in the price.
evidence.independence: Fed hike and dot plot: https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fed-hikes-hints-at-more-7-takeaways-from-the-september-fomc/ (2026-09). evidence.text: Peers that reported after Upstart last spoke show benign consumer credit and strong unsecured-loan demand. SoFi Q3 2026 personal-loan originations were a record $12.6bn (+69% YoY) with charge-offs down 34bp to 2.26%. Enova's NCO ratio fell to 8.1% from 8.5%. Happen (ex-LendingClub) beat, raised FY EPS to $1.87-1.92, and rose about 12% on 2026-10-29 ('we continue to outperform on credit'). OneMain's NCO rose modestly to 7.24% from 7.00%. Benign credit supports the loss curves Upstart's funding partners buy on and the contribution-margin path.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit-driven reactions: Nov 2025 -14.8% when the model 'overreacted' to macro and cut volume. No positive print has been credited to credit alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: UPST fell into these peer prints rather than rallying with Happen's +12%. If the benign credit read had transferred, UPST would not be at its 52-week low the week after. The market is treating UPST's problem as volume and take rate, not credit, so this finding is small.
evidence.independence: Happen: https://www.tikr.com/blog/happen-soars-12-on-earnings-beat-and-raised-outlook-we-continue-to-outperform-on-credit. evidence.text: 8-K of 2026-10-20: on 2026-10-16 Upstart Network entered a $200m senior secured 364-day revolver with MUFG at Term SOFR + 3.00%. It is secured on substantially all assets, carries covenants (minimum liquidity $100m, secured leverage of at most 2.5x), and is explicitly for general purposes and 'to fund the initial capitalization of Upstart Bank'. It matures 45 days after the bank's initial capitalization and is repaid from affiliate loan sales to the bank.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a corporate facility; the bank charter (OCC conditional approval, July 2026) produced a +5.8% day on the announcement.
evidence.why_not_priced: The quiet 8-K drew no wire coverage found. What the money buys: capitalizing Upstart Bank, which is corroborated by the conditional OCC approval and the early-2027 launch target, so this is not distress. Against that, borrowing secured to capitalize the bank, after $100m of H1 buybacks, says corporate cash is tight, and the bank is a cost centre with no 2026 revenue. Net zero; it resolves on the call if management updates bank timing, FDIC/Fed approvals or the 2027 expense line.
